conventions.convention: Use a fixed positively oriented inertial laboratory chart on R³ × R, right-handed cross products, SI units, c > 0, and ε₀ = (μ₀c²)⁻¹ > 0.

Amplitudes a: R³ ∖ {0} → C³ are smooth, compactly supported away from zero, and satisfy the bilinear condition k·a(k) = 0 without conjugation. A₊ uses normalization (2π)⁻³ᐟ² and phase exp(i(k·x − c|k|t)); A = 2 Re A₊, φ = 0, E = −∂ₜA, and B = curl A.

Whole-space integrals are componentwise limits of ordinary Riemann integrals over Q_R = [−R,R]³. Absolute integrability means a finite limit of the cube integrals of the sum of absolute real and imaginary components.

For n = k/|k|, helicity is the eigenvalue σ ∈ {+1,−1} of C(k)v = i n×v. P_σ = (P_T + σC)/2. The Hermitian product is conjugate-linear in its first argument. Rotation covariance is asserted for proper rotations only.

Angular momentum is relative to the fixed spatial origin. J_kin = ε₀∫x×(E×B), L_can = ε₀Σᵢ∫Eᵢ(x×∇)Aᵢ, and S_can = ε₀∫E×A. These functionals use the specified source-free Schwartz packet potentials; generic gauge transforms are outside their domain.

The finite-cube correction has positive volume term ε₀∫(div E)(x×A) and negative outward boundary term −ε₀∫(n·E)(x×A). Boundary integrals are sums of two-dimensional Riemann integrals over the six faces.

load_bearing.statement: Smooth compactly supported transverse amplitudes whose support avoids zero define real jointly smooth source-free vacuum Maxwell fields A, E, B with div A = 0 and φ = 0. At every fixed time these fields are Schwartz, their spatial Schwartz seminorms are bounded on compact time intervals, and their total field energy is finite.

For every nonzero k, P_T is the orthogonal projection onto T_k, C is Hermitian with C² = P_T and vanishes longitudinally, and P_σ = (P_T + σC)/2 gives complementary orthogonal rank-one helicity projections on T_k. Their multipliers preserve the compactly supported transverse amplitude class, commute with vacuum evolution and proper rotations, and are globally smooth away from zero; no global nonvanishing polarization vector is asserted.

For fixed-time real Schwartz vacuum packet fields and their specified Coulomb-gauge potential, the displayed J_kin, L_can, and S_can integrals are finite vectors with SI units J s. Their names do not identify separately gauge-invariant local densities.

For the specified source-free Schwartz packets, J_kin = L_can + S_can. More generally, for R > 0 and E,A restrictions of C¹ maps on a neighborhood of Q_R, with B = curl A, J_R = L_R + S_R + ε₀∫_{Q_R}(div E)(x×A) − ε₀∫_{∂Q_R}(n·E)(x×A). Absolute convergence and a vanishing boundary limit yield the corresponding whole-space identity retaining the divergence term.

seams_checked.note: The angular-spectrum definition explicitly preserves the supplier's compactly supported three-dimensional transverse amplitude convention and distinguishes it from fixed-frequency two-dimensional L² scalar data. Its consumers do not import finite packet energy or the canonical angular-momentum split into the scalar model. The supplier makes no reciprocal paraxial claim.

The bundle definition uses exactly C_n = i n×, P_σ = (P_T + σC_n)/2, and their smooth rank-one ranges. The rotation theorem retains the same helicity eigenvalue and proper active rotation convention, yielding exp(−iσα). Local frames and the separately proved global obstruction respect the supplier's explicit absence of a global polarization-vector assertion.
